B: Hello there! Rhys, is it? Martin. I think you're my last one, and I've been told all about your dog.
A: Oh no. Hiya. Yeah, Moss. She's, erm, she's sort of become a celebrity today, hasn't she?
B: The whippet that's scared of the bins! Lisa told me. I said to Karen, I'd carry it too, I'm soft as anything.
A: Ha. I thought my last call was my last call, to be honest, so this is a nice bonus.
B: Now, you're Welsh. Where abouts?
A: Caerphilly. Just outside Cardiff. I work in town.
B: My daughter's in Cardiff! Roath. She moved for work, she's in insurance, very sensible. I go up on the train and she takes me round all the coffee places, and I sit there with a flat white I don't want, pretending I'm cosmopolitan.
A: Roath's lovely, though. Loads of good food. There's a place by the park does brilliant brunch.
B: That's the one she drags me to, I bet. Eggs on something. What do you do, then? I had you down as a tech man, London sort of way, from your picture. No offence.
A: None taken, everyone's said that. Erm, video editor. Agency in Cardiff. Corporate films, ads. It's not very glamorous, mostly people in fleeces talking about synergy.
B: I'm in a fleece now!
A: Oh god, sorry. Not you. Different fleece.
B: Ha! Don't worry, I've been called worse by Year Nines. I was a geography teacher, thirty years near enough. Now I invigilate exams, sit in a sports hall glaring at people.
A: That's the map, then, behind you?
B: Exmoor, yeah. Do you get out walking at all?
A: Caerphilly Mountain with the dog most weekends. It's more of a hill, really. Erm, and I've got a road bike in the garage I keep meaning to use. Bought it in lockdown.
B: Everyone's got one of those! My son's got one in Bristol, it's got cobwebs on. We go to Pembrokeshire a lot, me and Karen, St Davids. Beautiful. I tried a bit of Welsh in a shop once and the woman just answered me in English, very kindly.
A: Ha, that's happened to me as well, to be honest. I understand a fair bit, but I go to pieces if someone's actually fluent.
B: No, see, you should give it a go! Nobody minds. I'm a folk man, I sing Welsh hymns at the pub sometimes, "Calon Lân", badly. Do you sing?
A: God, no. Erm... my nan did. Chapel. I've still got her hymn book, actually. Sorry, that's a bit random.
B: That's not random at all. Keep hold of that. My dad's things, I've got his old pocket knife, I'd not part with it for the world.
A: Yeah. Yeah, no, I won't. Erm, did you enjoy all this, the calls?
